statement: Whenever count_visited_nodes returns a result r, we have len(r) = n, and for every start i with 0 <= i < n the following holds. Define x_0(i)=i and x_{k+1}(i)=edges[x_k(i)] for k >= 0. Let m_i be the least positive integer m for which there exists j with 0 <= j < m and x_m(i)=x_j(i). Then r[i] = m_i. Equivalently, r[i] is the number of distinct nodes in the initial segment x_0(i), x_1(i), ..., x_{m_i-1}(i), i.e. the number visited before the first repeated node.
preconditions: Let n = len(edges). Assume 2 <= n <= 100000 and for every index i with 0 <= i < n, 0 <= edges[i] < n. Self-loops are allowed; see the note.

statement: Whenever count_visited_nodes returns a result r, len(r) = len(edges).
preconditions: Let n = len(edges). Assume 2 <= n <= 100000 and for every index i with 0 <= i < n, 0 <= edges[i] < n.

statement: Whenever count_visited_nodes returns a result r, for every i with 0 <= i < n, 1 <= r[i] <= n.
preconditions: Let n = len(edges). Assume 2 <= n <= 100000 and for every index i with 0 <= i < n, 0 <= edges[i] < n.

statement: Under these preconditions, count_visited_nodes returns a result r; it does not fail due to arithmetic overflow, out-of-bounds access, or panic.
preconditions: Let n = len(edges). Assume 2 <= n <= 100000 and for every index i with 0 <= i < n, 0 <= edges[i] < n.

statement: Whenever count_visited_nodes returns a result r, for every i with 0 <= i < n, if edges[i] = i then r[i] = 1.
preconditions: Let n = len(edges). Assume 2 <= n <= 100000 and for every index i with 0 <= i < n, 0 <= edges[i] < n.

statement: Whenever count_visited_nodes returns a result r, for all i and j with 0 <= i < n and 0 <= j < n, if i != j, edges[i] = j, and edges[j] = i, then r[i] = 2 and r[j] = 2.
preconditions: Let n = len(edges). Assume 2 <= n <= 100000 and for every index i with 0 <= i < n, 0 <= edges[i] < n.

statement: Whenever count_visited_nodes returns a result r, for every i with 0 <= i < n, define x_0(i)=i and x_{k+1}(i)=edges[x_k(i)] for k >= 0. If there exists k >= 1 with x_k(i)=i, then r[i] equals the least such k.
preconditions: Let n = len(edges). Assume 2 <= n <= 100000 and for every index i with 0 <= i < n, 0 <= edges[i] < n.

statement: Whenever count_visited_nodes returns a result r, for every i with 0 <= i < n, define x_0(i)=i and x_{k+1}(i)=edges[x_k(i)] for k >= 0. If for all k >= 1, x_k(i) != i, then r[i] = r[edges[i]] + 1.
preconditions: Let n = len(edges). Assume 2 <= n <= 100000 and for every index i with 0 <= i < n, 0 <= edges[i] < n.

statement: Whenever count_visited_nodes returns a result r, for every i with 0 <= i < n, define x_0(i)=i and x_{k+1}(i)=edges[x_k(i)] for k >= 0. If there exists k >= 1 with x_k(edges[i]) = i, then r[i] = r[edges[i]]; otherwise r[i] = r[edges[i]] + 1.
preconditions: Let n = len(edges). Assume 2 <= n <= 100000 and for every index i with 0 <= i < n, 0 <= edges[i] < n.

statement: Whenever count_visited_nodes returns a result r, for all i and j with 0 <= i < n and 0 <= j < n, define x_0(i)=i and x_{k+1}(i)=edges[x_k(i)] for k >= 0. If there exist a >= 0 and b >= 0 such that x_a(i)=j and x_b(j)=i, then r[i] = r[j].
preconditions: Let n = len(edges). Assume 2 <= n <= 100000 and for every index i with 0 <= i < n, 0 <= edges[i] < n.

statement: Whenever count_visited_nodes returns a result r, for every i with 0 <= i < n, define x_0(i)=i and x_{k+1}(i)=edges[x_k(i)] for k >= 0. If for all k >= 1, x_k(i) != i, then r[i] > r[edges[i]].
preconditions: Let n = len(edges). Assume 2 <= n <= 100000 and for every index i with 0 <= i < n, 0 <= edges[i] < n.

statement: Whenever count_visited_nodes returns a result r, define x_0(i)=i and x_{k+1}(i)=edges[x_k(i)] for k >= 0. If for every i with 0 <= i < n the least positive k satisfying x_k(i)=i exists and equals n, then r[i] = n for every i with 0 <= i < n.
preconditions: Let n = len(edges). Assume 2 <= n <= 100000 and for every index i with 0 <= i < n, 0 <= edges[i] < n.

statement: Whenever count_visited_nodes returns a result r, for every i with 0 <= i < n, r[i] >= 2.
preconditions: Let n = len(edges). Assume 2 <= n <= 100000 and for every index i with 0 <= i < n, 0 <= edges[i] < n. Suppose additionally that edges[i] != i for every i with 0 <= i < n.

statement: Whenever count_visited_nodes returns a result r, for every i with 0 <= i < n, if r[i] = 1 then edges[i] = i.
preconditions: Let n = len(edges). Assume 2 <= n <= 100000 and for every index i with 0 <= i < n, 0 <= edges[i] < n.

statement: Whenever count_visited_nodes returns a result r, for all i and j with 0 <= i < n and 0 <= j < n, define x_0(i)=i and x_{k+1}(i)=edges[x_k(i)] for k >= 0. If there exists a >= 0 with x_a(i)=j, then r[i] >= r[j]. Moreover, equality holds for distinct i and j exactly when there also exists b >= 0 with x_b(j)=i.
preconditions: Let n = len(edges). Assume 2 <= n <= 100000 and for every index i with 0 <= i < n, 0 <= edges[i] < n.
